articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Condition Monitoring and Failure Diagnosis: II' (Digest No.102)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Condition Monitoring and Failure Diagnosis: II
IEE Colloquium on Condition Monitoring and Failure Diagnosis: II
abstract: Current industrial networks rely heavily on the carrier sense multiple access collision detection (CSMA/CD) network access technique. Such access schemes are classified as stochastic, due to the inability to directly assign a time for the transmission of data traffic between sender and receiver equipment. A deterministic network structure is introduced that overcomes the unpredictable nature of CSMA/CD networks. The network is based on the ring topology and is of a robust design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Condition monitoring of motorised valve actuators and similar intermittently operated devices
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Condition Monitoring and Failure Diagnosis: II
abstract: The author describes work done to identify a simple method of measuring the condition of motorised valve actuators and similar intermittently operated power output devices. By analysing the movement as a command is executed, it is possible to derive a signature descriptive of the actuator or system under investigation. This signature can then be compared with subsequent signatures as the device wears, and eventually used to establish the maintenance intervals applicable to a particular duty.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Signal processing within a real time AI architecture for condition monitoring and fault diagnosis
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Condition Monitoring and Failure Diagnosis: II
abstract: The authors present a method for diagnosing faults based on signal processing of signals from conventional sensors taking measurements from a dynamic system. This ensures that no disruption is applied to the system in fitting 'conditioning sensors'. The method is based on the techniques of system identification and Kalman filtering in which the faults are diagnosed by checking the Kalman filter residuals against previously 'learnt' patterns.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Condition monitoring of HV plant within South of Scotland Electricity Board
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Condition Monitoring and Failure Diagnosis: II
abstract: The South of Scotland Electricity Board (SSEB) operates 15 main power stations, of which three are nuclear, five are fossil fired and the remainder are hydro electric. In each of these stations, there are many high voltage electric motors as well as the main generators. The benefits of a regular programme of HV NDT have been identified for some time, and all such machines now have an HV 'fingerprint' against which each machine's performance is measured on a regular basis. The author describes the tests which are carried out on the SSEB HV Plant, and the equipment used for this purpose. In addition, he describes the future proposals of SSEB in this area, involving the application of remote communications and Expert Systems technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Detecting faults in fermentation processes, with an example using analytical redundancy
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Condition Monitoring and Failure Diagnosis: II
abstract: The authors review some of the requirements of the fermentation industry for the detection of faults in fermentation processes. They review applications ranging from expert systems to model-based analytical redundancy. They also use techniques of analytical redundancy on biochemical reactor models and fermentation mass balances and brief results of this work are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
